title: Neuro-ophthalmology, pupils and cranial neuropathies

steps.tx: Asymmetric anterior visual pathway lesions alter pupillary reactivity during dynamic light testing. A relative afferent **pupillary defect**, historically known as a **Marcus Gunn** pupil, is elicited by the swinging flashlight test when paradoxical dilatation occurs as light swings from the unaffected eye to the diseased optic nerve.

steps.tx: Sympathetic pathway interruptions produce characteristic oculosympathetic paresis in clinical neurology. **Horner syndrome** results from disruption of the three-neuron oculosympathetic tract, displaying the classic ipsilateral triad of pupillary **miosis**, mild superior eyelid ptosis and lower lid elevation from sympathetic denervation, and facial anhidrosis.

Horner syndrome results from disruption of the three-neuron oculosympathetic tract, displaying the classic ipsilateral triad of pupillary miosis, mild superior eyelid ptosis and lower lid elevation from sympathetic denervation, and facial anhidrosis.

left.title: Horner Syndrome Triad
points: Pupillary miosis due to dilator paresis
Partial ptosis from Müller muscle weakness
Apparent enophthalmos due to narrowed fissure
Anhidrosis depending on anatomical lesion level

right.title: Pharmacological Testing
points: Apraclonidine (0.5%) reverses anisocoria
Cocaine (10%) fails to dilate affected pupil
Hydroxyamphetamine (1%) localises third-order
Normal pupil dilates, Horner pupil stays small

steps.tx: Anatomical localization along the oculosympathetic chain dictates sweat gland involvement. First-order central neuron pathways traverse from the posterior hypothalamus down the brainstem to the **ciliospinal center** of Budge at C8-T2, while third-order postganglionic fibres distal to the superior cervical ganglion travel along the internal carotid artery, sparing facial sweating along the external carotid territory of the **oculosympathetic** pathway.

steps.tx: Parasympathetic postganglionic denervation causes persistent internal ophthalmoplegia. An **Adie tonic pupil** arises from inflammatory degeneration of the ciliary ganglion, producing an enlarged, poorly reactive pupil with near-light dissociation and marked denervation supersensitivity manifesting as brisk constriction to dilute **pilocarpine** at 0.125% concentration.

steps.tx: Specific midbrain tegmental neurosyphilitic lesions produce pathognomonic bilateral pupillary changes. **Argyll Robertson** pupils present as small, irregular, bilateral pupils that do not react to direct or consensual light stimulation but constrict briskly to accommodation, establishing classic **light-near dissociation** in central nervous system neurosyphilis.

left.title: Argyll Robertson Pupil
points: Bilateral small, irregular pupils
Absent response to light stimulation
Brisk, intact response to near accommodation
Associated with tabes dorsalis and neurosyphilis

right.title: Adie Tonic Pupil
points: Unilateral dilated pupil in young females
Tonic delayed slow redilation after near effort
Segmental vermiform pupillary border palsy
Constricts to 0.125% dilute pilocarpine

steps.tx: Extrinsic compression of midline visual pathways produces pathognomonic visual field amputations. Complete **Bitemporal hemianopia** results from mechanical compression of decussating nasal retinal crossing fibres at the central **optic chiasm**, most frequently precipitated by expanding pituitary macroadenomas, tuberculum sellae meningiomas, or craniopharyngiomas.

rows: Temporal lobectomy, MCA inferior division stroke

steps.tx: Temporal lobe pathway disruptions selectively sacrifice superior visual quadrants. An incongruous or congruous homonymous superior **quadrantanopia**, colloquially termed a pie-in-the-sky defect, is caused by contralateral temporal lobe lesions disrupting the anteriorly sweeping **Meyer loop** fibres as they loop around the temporal ventricular horn.

steps.tx: Acute oculomotor nerve dysfunction demands rigorous emergent vascular exclusion. An **Oculomotor** third nerve palsy presenting with complete pupillary dilatation and unresponsiveness signals external mechanical compression, mandating emergency exclusion of an expanding **posterior communicating artery** saccular aneurysm prior to fatal subarachnoid rupture.

left.title: Compressive Third Nerve Palsy
points: Dilated non-reactive blown pupil
Superficial dorsomedial parasympathetics crushed
Expanding PCOM aneurysm until proven otherwise
Mandatory urgent CTA or digital subtraction angiogram

right.title: Microvascular Ischaemic Palsy
points: Pupil completely spared and briskly reactive
Ischaemia of central core nerve trunk
Diabetic or hypertensive microangiopathy
Spontaneous recovery within 6 to 12 weeks
